title: Word Search II
statement: You get a grid of lowercase letters and a list of words. A word is on the grid if you can spell it by moving between side-by-side cells, never using the same cell twice in one word. Return every word from the list that is on the grid, each one once, in any order.

example.caption: Board o a t / e t h, words oat and oath. Both start with o-a-t, so one walk through the grid finds both.

idea.sentence: Put all the words in one trie and walk the grid once with it, so every step checks all words together and a path that no word starts with is dropped at once.

jargon.plain: A tree where each edge is one letter, so words with the same start share nodes.
Stop exploring a branch early because it cannot lead to an answer.
Try a path, and when it is finished, undo your marks and step back to try another path.

watch.inputHint: Two arguments: the board as rows of single letters, then the word list, e.g. [["o","a"],["e","t"]], ["oat"]

vars.meaning: number of cells on the board

compare.bruteLabel: Search the whole board once per word
compare.optimalLabel: One walk, all words at once via the trie
compare.unit: work, growing with the number of words

rows.name: One search per word
rows.note: Every word repeats its own search from every cell.

rows.name: Trie + DFS
rows.note: One walk covers all words. Paths nobody starts with are cut off at once, so in practice it explores far less.

fast.takeaway: The trie turns a question asked once per word into one question for all words together. Pruning on a missing child is what makes it fast.

stages.title: Build the trie
stages.note: Insert every word into one trie and mark where each word ends.

stages.title: Step onto a cell
stages.note: If the trie has a child for this cell's letter, extend the path, mark the cell used and look at its neighbours.

stages.title: Prune
stages.note: If the trie has no child for this letter, no word starts with this path. Return without going deeper.

stages.title: Word found
stages.note: If the node ends a word, record the path and clear the flag so the word is reported only once.

stages.title: Backtrack
stages.note: After all neighbours, unmark the cell so other paths can use it.

edges.title: Cell used twice
edges.why: The third letter would need the first cell again. The used mark blocks it.

edges.title: Same word, many paths
edges.input: board of all a, word aa
edges.why: Many paths spell it. Clearing the end flag after the first find keeps the answer free of duplicates.

edges.title: Word inside another
edges.input: words ab and abc on a b c
edges.why: ab ends on the way to abc. Record it and keep walking, do not stop at the first word end.

edges.title: No words
edges.why: The trie has no children, so every cell is pruned at once. Return an empty list, not null.

gotchas.text: Do not stop the walk when you find a word. A longer word may continue along the same path, like oat and oath.
Unmark the cell when you backtrack. If the used mark stays, later paths wrongly think that cell is taken.
Clear the end flag after reporting a word. Otherwise a word with several paths is added several times.
Use a Map for the children. A plain object breaks on keys like "constructor" or "__proto__".
With [26]*node arrays the index is letter - 'a'. Board cells here are strings, so take board[r][c][0] first. A letter outside a to z would index out of range.
Start found as []string{}, not var found []string. A nil slice becomes null in JSON when there is no answer.
A recursive closure must be declared first (var dfs func(...)) and assigned after, or it cannot call itself.

recap.key: Walk the grid once with a trie of all words. Cut a path when the trie has no child for the next letter.
recap.complexity: O(m * 4^L) worst case, much less with pruning. Space O(total letters).
moves: Insert all words into one trie
DFS from every cell, following trie children
No child for this letter: prune
Word end: record it and clear the flag. Unmark on the way back
